item.title: Real Madrid closely monitoring Premier League goalkeeper as potential Courtois successor
item.description: Real Madrid closely monitoring Premier League goalkeeper as potential Courtois successor Real Madrid have been fortunate to have a goalkeeper like Thibaut Courtois, who has been a beacon of consistency for the club over the years. However, at 34, the club are also right to start preparing for his eventual successor as part of their long-term planning. Now, according to journalist Ben Fernandes Santos , Real Madrid are closely monitoring Brighton & Hove Albion goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen as a possible replacement. The 24-year-old Dutch international has made a name for himself with impressive performances in the Premier League. Real Madrid tracking Verbruggen Verbruggen’s latest performance against Manchester City yesterday was a display worthy of the Hall of Fame against one of the league’s best attacks. He made seven saves as Fabian Hurzeler’s side kept an incredible clean sheet and secured a win at the Etihad Stadium. Verbruggen has developed considerably since joining Brighton from Anderlecht in 2023. He quickly became first choice at the Amex and for the Netherlands. Bart Verbruggen is developing into an excellent goalkeeper. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) His impressive reflexes, composure under pressure and ability to distribute the ball effectively make him the perfect modern-day goalkeeper. Madrid have been monitoring the 24-year-old for some time now and continue to track his progress for the Seagulls. Courtois succession becoming a long-term priority Courtois is still going strong at 34, remains Jose Mourinho’s undisputed first-choice goalkeeper and has a contract that runs until 2027. The Belgian is also in talks with the club over a potential extension , underlining his intention to continue as the club’s number one. As long as he continues to perform without a drop in his level, there is no reason for Madrid to think about replacing Courtois. However, identifying his future successor instead of waiting until he leaves is a smart and sensible decision by Los Blancos . Could Verbruggen be the answer to Madrid’s life after Courtois? (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Replacing Courtois is not just about finding another shot-stopper. Mourinho will want someone capable of handling pressure, commanding the penalty area and delivering consistently. Verbruggen may still have areas of his game that he needs to improve, but at 24, he is still very young for a goalkeeper. If he continues on the same trajectory in the Premier League, it is only a matter of time before top teams in Europe start queuing up for him. It remains to be seen how Verbruggen develops and whether he inherits the No. 1 jersey from Thibaut Courtois at the Santiago Bernabeu in the future.

item.title: Jake Paul teases Canelo Alvarez and makes vow after Mexican’s winning return
item.description: Jake Paul has set his sights on a fight with Canelo Alvarez after the Mexican made his return to the ring with a win over Christian Mbilli. Competing for the first time in 13 months, the Mexican won by a unanimous points decision after a hard-fought battle in Riyadh, absorbing plenty of punishment from Mbilli to win back the WBC super-middleweight title. The encounter had gone ahead in Saudi Arabia despite continuing tensions in the Middle East, and marked a significant success for the Mexican having suffered only the third defeat of his career in his last bout with Terence Crawford in September of last year. Paul, the YouTuber-turned-boxer, was an interested observer and was impressed by Canelo – before vowing that the pair will fight at some point. “Out of the ring for 13 months but still the same old Canelo. Respect,” he said on social media. “[He] did take a lot of punches though. We will dance my friend, we will dance.” The two boxers previously came close to fighting in early 2025 before Canelo signed a four-fight deal with Saudi promoter Turki Alashikh. Paul has confirmed that he will return to the ring for the first time since losing to Anthony Joshua with a fight on Christmas Eve in Dubai . His opponent is as yet unconfirmed.

item.description: The Golden State Valkyries celebrate after the team's victory over the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center, Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, in San Francisco. (Santiago Mejia/S.F. Chronicle) Breathtakingly fast. Historically impactful. Incredibly, improbably and spectacularly: WNBA champions. Seventeen months, two weeks and one day after they played their very first game, the Golden State Valkyries raised the WNBA championship trophy. It is the fastest a North American professional sports team has ever won a title. "It's insane," said Joe Lacob, the man who set the bar at five years and saw the Valkyries clear it with three years to spare. Insane, perhaps, but what happened Halloween night in a packed, joyous Chase Center also felt inevitable. The Valkyries have made history with every step of their rocketship ride. There were 18,000 true believers in the building and millions more scattered around the globe, from San Francisco to Paris to Italy to Taiwan to Japan. And the overwhelming sense was that there was no way that this wasn't going to be a happy, beautiful ending. "For all the people that have been underrated, misunderstood, this is for y'all," coach Natalie Nakase said. "This is proof. If you put all your heart and soul in, you f-ing win championships." And the Valkyries did. Playing the first Game 7 in WNBA history, the last game was much like the previous six against the Atlanta Dream: a defensive, physical grinder of a game. The Valkyries' offense was clunky in the first half, Gabby Williams was invisible, and the Valkyries trailed the Dream by six. The building was getting a little nervous. But then something unlocked in Williams and she became unstoppable , doing things on the court that we've usually seen from No. 30 on the men's side. She scored 28 second-half points and led her team to victory. She was named the MVP of the game. In a beer-soaked, profanity-filled postgame press conference that jumped from team bonding to wine preference to Nakase's father to questions in French, Nakase was eventually asked a basketball strategy question about adjustments. "Y'all think I know what I'm doing!" she exclaimed. Actually, yes we do. Nakase, the first woman coach of color to win a WNBA championship, not only coached the hell out of this team, she helped bind them into an unshakable unit. Williams, who brought the French national team to within a basket of the gold medal, who finished runner-up to the United States again in last summer's FIBA World Cup, who never felt she was fully appreciated by her other WNBA teams, found a home with Nakase and the Valkyries. "Sometimes the best thing is right in front of you, the people who love you, who you love," Williams said. "That's what got me going tonight, going all season… I walked into a group full of love and that just changed the entire trajectory of my career." That's the beauty of the Valkyries. item.title: Arsenal target end to Anfield hoodoo as Liverpool visit offers chance to go top
item.description: Arsenal target end to Anfield hoodoo as Liverpool visit offers chance to go top Arsenal head to Liverpool in the Premier League this afternoon with a place at the top of the table the prize at stake. Defeat for Manchester City on Saturday means the Gunners will take the lead in the title race, if defeat is avoided at Anfield. Liverpool, meanwhile, will want a win that could see Andoni Iraola's improving team close the gap to the top to just three points. Trips to Liverpool have not been fruitful for Arsenal in recent seasons. The Gunners have not won at Anfield in the Premier League since September 2012, when goals from Lukas Podolski and Santi Cazorla earned Arsenal an early-season win on the road. Mikel Arteta was in midfield for Arsenal the last time the North Londoners earned a league win at Liverpool, with the club's record since then making for grim reading. Arsenal are winless in their last 13 league visits to Liverpool (D5 L8). However, Arsenal have never gone 14 games at Anfield without a win, with their previous 13-game winless run broken by a historic 2-0 final-day victory in the 1988-89 season that snatched the Division 1 title from their opponents. Arsenal also have a good recent record against Liverpool overall. The Gunners have lost just once in the last eight meetings in all competitions, when Dominik Szoboszlai's stunning free-kick sealed a 1-0 win for Liverpool last season. Arteta says chance to end Anfield record is an opportunity for Arsenal Ahead of the game, Arteta called the clash an opportunity for his side to break an unwanted record. "It’s an opportunity. I came here [to Arsenal] and in many places we were 20, 22 years, 18 years without winning, and we’ve been doing all these things, so on Sunday, that’s the opportunity that we have," he said. "We're going there with full conviction; that's number one, and we've been very, very close in the last few years to win. But something is missed, and that's what we've been discussing the last few days. To go there with a real purpose. To hurt them and get away from there with a victory."

item.title: Injury crisis! Bayern Munich face major Der Klassiker fallout as Ismael Saibari leaves on crutches & Serge Gnabry suffers setback
item.description: FC Bayern München v Borussia Dortmund - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Bayern Munich’s dramatic 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund has come at a massive cost as the Bundesliga leaders contend with a growing injury list. The Bavarian giants saw multiple key players forced off during the high-stakes encounter, leaving their attacking options severely depleted for the upcoming Champions League fixtures. Saibari and Gnabry facing lengthy spells out The immediate aftermath of the stalemate against Dortmund has been overshadowed by serious concerns regarding the fitness of Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry. Saibari, who was a constant threat throughout the match, was seen leaving the stadium on crutches following a painful collision. The Moroccan international appeared to twist his ankle during a frantic sequence in the box after BVB goalkeeper Gregor Kobel denied him from close range. Gnabry’s situation is equally troubling for the coaching staff. The experienced winger was forced off just two minutes after Saibari’s exit, appearing to suffer a muscle-related setback that could keep him sidelined for several weeks. Sporting director Max Eberl did little to calm the nerves of the Bayern faithful when addressing the media shortly after the final whistle. "Both injuries are somewhat larger, without me being able to give the prognosis or the diagnosis right now, they will do that first, but it looks like both are larger," he said, as quoted by BILD . Olise limp adds to Kompany's selection headache The fitness concerns did not end with the primary substitutions, as Michael Olise was also spotted limping heavily as he made his way to the team bus. The French playmaker completed the match but appeared to be in significant discomfort once the adrenaline of the contest had worn off. Bayern are hopeful that his issue is less severe than those suffered by his teammates, though uncertainty remains high. "With Olise, we currently think we feel that it's not that bad, but it's relatively difficult to say that even after such games, shortly afterwards with the adrenaline. But let's assume that it's not that bad," Eberl explained when asked about the former Crystal Palace man. Eberl admits situation is feeling heavy With the medical room now at full capacity, there is a palpable sense of frustration within the Bayern camp. The club had hoped to use the Dortmund game as a springboard for a dominant run of form, but they must now pivot to damage control. The lack of attacking depth could force tactical shifts or the promotion of youth prospects to fill the gaps left by Saibari and Gnabry. Eberl admitted that the sheer volume of setbacks is becoming difficult to manage for the club’s hierarchy. "At the moment it feels a bit heavy, what is happening around us," the sporting director confessed. item.title: Third-choice? Inside Alexander-Arnold's struggles in Madrid
item.description: Alexander-Arnold has featured in seven of the 13 matches Real Madrid have played so far this season, starting four times and registering one assist [Getty Images] It has not been an easy start to the season for Trent Alexander-Arnold. The full-back joined Real Madrid in June 2025 with the ambition of establishing himself as the club's first-choice right-back, but the reality has been very different. The arrival of Denzel Dumfries from Inter Milan this summer added more competition in the position, and now manager Jose Mourinho appears to be favouring Fede Valverde, normally a midfielder, as a starter at right-back. It leaves Alexander-Arnold as third choice and leads to questions on where, and in what role, Mourinho sees the England international's future. Alexander-Arnold has participated in seven of the 13 games Real have played this season, though he has only started four times and has made just one assist - in a 4-0 home win over Malaga. And his involvement has notably declined over the past four games - he did not play against Roma, Sevilla or RB Leipzig and got just a couple of minutes in the Clasico, when he came on in stoppage time. Alexander-Arnold has just turned 28 and Real showed how much they wanted him last summer by paying 10m euros (£8.33m) to secure his early release and make him available for the Club World Cup, rather than wait until he was available on a free transfer when his Liverpool contract expired. But, despite having a contract until 2031, his future now hangs in the balance. 'A dream come true' Alexander-Arnold made an excellent first impression at the club, winning over supporters during his first public appearance by delivering his arrival speech in Spanish and saying signing for Real was a "dream come true". "I'm very happy and proud to be here. I'm eager to show the club and the fans what I can do," he added. There was considerable optimism surrounding Alexander-Arnold's arrival, with his signing appearing to form part of the club's succession plan at right-back - he could provide cover for Dani Carvajal while positioning himself as a potential long-term successor to the veteran Spaniard. His first season, however, fell short of expectations. He made 21 La Liga appearances in 2025-26 out of a possible 38, with 14 starts, as injuries and a lack of continuity prevented Alexander-Arnold from establishing himself as a regular presence. item.title: Achraf Hakimi REJECTS early PSG contract approach as Moroccan star stalls talks
item.description: FBL-FRA-LIGUE1-LE HAVRE-PSG - AFP Achraf Hakimi has stalled early negotiations over a new Paris Saint-Germain contract after the club made an initial approach to his representatives. The Moroccan defender remains happy in the French capital but sees no immediate rush to sign an extension. Hakimi stalls PSG contract approach Hakimi has enjoyed an exceptional start to the current campaign for PSG. His consistently impressive form has firmly reinforced his status as a fundamental pillar of the club's ambitious sporting project. As a direct result of these strong performances, the Parisian hierarchy want to secure the Moroccan's long-term future. The club recently made a preliminary approach to his representatives to test the waters regarding a new contract. However, this initial advance did not lead to the desired discussions. According to L’Equipe , Hakimi's entourage effectively paused the club's initiative, opting against opening formal negotiations at this early stage. No rush to sign new deal The decision to stall talks is not rooted in financial demands or the proposed length of the new contract. Instead, Hakimi and his representatives simply believe there is plenty of time left before a new deal becomes necessary. The full-back already signed a contract extension two years ago, and his current terms run until June 2029. Consequently, he feels absolutely no urgency to sit down at the negotiating table just yet. PSG want to act proactively to protect one of their most valuable assets on a long-term basis. However, the player evidently prefers to bide his time before committing to a fresh agreement. Defender thriving under Enrique Hakimi currently finds himself in an incredibly comfortable position in the French capital. He remains an indispensable figure for manager Luis Enrique and continues to thrive under the Spaniard's tactical guidance. The talented defender recently underlined his immense sporting influence by delivering a historic performance on the pitch, including his recent hat-trick in a resounding 5-1 victory over Le Havre in Ligue 1.. With several years still remaining on his current deal, he holds all the leverage regarding his future. Contract talks put on hold Both parties still share a mutual desire to continue their successful journey together. They simply operate on completely different timelines when it comes to formalising the next step. The lack of immediate pressure from either side means this contractual matter is unlikely to progress quickly. The situation is now expected to remain completely dormant for the next several months.

item.title: 'The performance was spot on!' – Aaron Danks reacts to fresh Bayern injury nightmare
item.description: FC Bayern München v Borussia Dortmund - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks praised his team's execution and control despite suffering three fresh injury setbacks during their 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund. Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, and Michael Olise were all forced off during a punishing Klassiker encounter. Danks manages squad through chaotic Klassiker Interim head coach Aaron Danks took charge of Bayern Munich once again in the absence of Vincent Kompany for Saturday's top-of-the-table Klassiker against Borussia Dortmund. The match ended in a dramatic 2-2 draw following Fabio Silva's 90th-minute equalizer. The fixture took a heavy physical toll on Bayern's depleted squad at the Allianz Arena. Danks was forced into multiple tactical re-adjustments due to mid-match fitness setbacks. Triple injury blow hits Bavarian rotation Bayern's existing injury list grew significantly as Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry were both forced off during the first half. Saibari suffered an injury while following up his saved shot, with Gnabry limping off minutes later. To compound matters, winger Michael Olise was also substituted late in the match after picking up a knock. Nathaniel Brown and Josip Stanisic were thrust into action early to steady the framework. Danks remains proud of tactical execution Despite the chaotic circumstances, Danks praised the team's tactical discipline and overall game control . "It’s mixed feeling. We’re very pleased with our performance, especially in the second half. We had good control of the game," Danks noted. "Dortmund have a good defensive balance, but I think we found lots of ways today to create chances." "Obviously we’re disappointed in the end that we didn’t win, but I can tell the players that the performance was spot on. We did a lot right," the Englishman affirmed. Depleted Bayern prepare for European test Full-back Nathaniel Brown echoed Danks' sentiment, admitting the early substitutions made the first half difficult to navigate. Bayern maintain their lead at the top of the Bundesliga table ahead of Dortmund on goal difference. item.title: Jose Mourinho makes key midfield decision for Real Madrid against Racing Santander – report
item.description: Jose Mourinho makes key midfield decision for Real Madrid against Racing Santander – report Real Madrid have seen their midfield undergo an important transformation in recent weeks following tactical tweaks from Jose Mourinho. The Portuguese manager spent the first couple of months of the season without finding the right balance in midfield. However, the emergence of Bernardo Silva as a central figure and his partnership with Aurelien Tchouameni have been fruitful for Los Blancos . According to MARCA (h/t Madrid Zone ), Jose Mourinho is expected to maintain that continuity and start Bernardo and Tchouameni as the double pivot against Racing Santander. Bernardo Silva and Tchouameni set to lead Madrid’s midfield The decision would see Mourinho continue with a midfield combination that offers complementary qualities: Bernardo’s technical control and Tchouameni’s defensive prowess. The Frenchman has always thrived at the base of midfield, using his physical presence and ball-winning ability to disrupt opposition attacks. What he is not that comfortable doing is being tasked with progressing the ball. That is where Bernardo Silva comes in. Aurelien Tchouameni is an expert at doing the dirty work in midfield. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The Portuguese midfielder is very comfortable with the ball at his feet and can support Tchouameni effectively in that role. With Jude Bellingham further ahead in midfield and Arda Guler on the right flank, the set-up gives Madrid much better control in midfield. Mourinho’s new midfield formula faces another test The impact of Bernardo Silva’s inclusion in the starting line-up is best captured by one statistic comparing games with and without him. Excluding El Clasico , Los Blancos have averaged 57% possession in games with Bernardo and 47% in games without him. This illustrates the kind of control the Portuguese midfielder can add to the team better than any words can. Bernardo Silva has had a transformative effect on Real Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) While possession also depends on the kind of opposition and the game state, there is no doubt that the former Manchester City star has had a role to play. The new midfield partnership now faces another test against Jose Alberto’s Racing Santander, who will look to play aggressively. It is good to see Mourinho looking to maintain continuity with a formula that seems to be rewarding the team with success. It remains to be seen whether the duo start in the official line-up and how they fare at El Sardinero later tonight.

item.title: Barcelona star makes a strong statement after a disappointing week – “Happy to help with assists”
item.description: Barcelona star makes a strong statement after a disappointing week – “Happy to help with assists” It has been well-documented that last week was a terrible one for Barcelona as they suffered back to back defeats to rivals PSG and Real Madrid. It was a worse one for Fermin Lopez, who was a mere substitute against PSG and struggled to impact the game in the Clasico against Real Madrid. However, Fermin appears to have repaid Hansi Flick’s faith with a solid display of dominance in Barcelona’s 6-1 win over Alaves. A clear MVP against Alaves It was an attacking masterclass from Fermin Lopez. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Fermin was the undisputed MVP against Alaves, as he chipped in with one goal and two assists, meaning he was directly involved in three of the six goals. The Spanish international made his mark early on, playing a key role in Raphinha’s opener as he capitalized from an excellent ball from Pedri. Fermin then got on to the scoresheet himself with a sublime finish to make it 2-0 for Barcelona around the 23rd minute mark. His final goal involvement saw him win the ball back in an aggressive press, as he once again set up Raphinha’s second goal of the night. Overall, it was a top-notch display from Fermin, who has now racked up six goals and six assists in all competitions, making him one of the most productive players at Barcelona apart from Lamine Yamal and Raphinha. Fermin delighted with the performance Fermin himself was delighted with his and Barcelona’s performance against Alaves, when reflecting on it after the game. Fermin has been involved in 12 goals this season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “It was a difficult week for us; we couldn’t win two very high-level, very demanding matches and I think there was no better way or setting to turn things around than at the Camp Nou and in front of our fans ,” he said (h/t Mundo Deportivo ). “We played a good game, we found ourselves again, we managed to recover our identity and our true level and now we must continue playing this way,” he added. When asked about his contributions, Fermin said he was happy to help the team in whatever capacity, adding that he was completely exhausted as Flick had no avenue of subbing him off. “I have to keep being happy to help the team with assists,” he said. “Flick told me, even though he knew I was done, that he was going to substitute de Jong and that I should hang on a bit and try to relax ,” he concluded.

item.title: Ohio State Coach Ryan Day Places Blame for Upset Loss to USC
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 31: Head coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes walks out of the tunnel before the game against the USC Trojans at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) Getty The No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes entered Saturday night’s road matchup against the USC Trojans knowing they couldn’t put all the pressure on true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey. And they ultimately failed to do that. The special teams struggled, and the defense couldn’t get off the field without allowing points as USC won 30-18 to pull off the upset and hand the Buckeyes their second loss of the season. The offense, with Fahey commanding it, wasn’t perfect, as they stalled out several times in USC territory. But all in all, asking him to go out and put the team on his back and win the game wasn’t realistic. And it seemed that’s what Ohio State tried to do Saturday night. Ryan Day Places Blame for Loss Speaking to the media after the game, Ryan Day was quite blunt about why Ohio State lost, and it wasn’t Fahey. Day made it clear that there were simply too many costly mistakes. He blamed the loss on “too many penalties” and failing to execute in the red zone. Ryan Day said there were “just way too many mistakes” in Ohio State’s loss to USC, and said the Buckeyes needed to do more as a team to support Luke Fahey in his first start. https://t.co/E1Fp100FWU — Eleven Warriors (@11W) November 1, 2026 Fahey ended the game completing 21 of 28 passes for 260 yards and one touchdown. The Buckeyes rushed for 204 yards on the ground as a team. They totaled over 460 yards collectively on offense but having just 18 points to show for it. Jeremiah Smith led all Buckeyes wide receivers with 10 receptions for 83 yards and a touchdown. Looking at Ohio State It’s safe to say the Buckeyes’ season is now firmly on life support with two losses. Ohio State will get to head back home to Columbus this week for a matchup against the Oregon Ducks. After that, they’ll finish off the regular season with matchups against Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan. They’ll likely have to win out to remain in the College Football Playoff picture. LaNorris Sellers gave NFL scouts plenty to think about on Saturday, and the South Carolina football quarterback wasted little time showing why he has first-round potential against Oklahoma. With the game scoreless in the first quarter at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium, Sellers took off on a 15-yard touchdown run to give the Gamecocks a 7-0 lead on their third drive of the afternoon. It was only the beginning of a huge day for the junior. Sellers completed 19 of 24 passes for a season-high 301 yards and three touchdowns, with two interceptions. He also ran for 96 yards and two scores on 13 carries, finishing with 397 total yards and five total touchdowns as South Carolina cruised to a 42-25 win over the Sooners in Norman . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sellers’ highlights were not limited to the ground. After Oklahoma’s Kip Lewis tied the game with a 30-yard pick-six, Christian Clark put South Carolina back in front with a 1-yard run. With the Gamecocks up 14-7 in the second quarter, Sellers stepped up in the pocket on third-and-12 and launched an 84-yard touchdown pass to DJ Black. He then hit Nyck Harbor for a score before halftime to send South Carolina into the break up 28-10, and later found Mazeo Bennett Jr. for a 79-yard touchdown. The Gamecocks dominated from start to finish. They outgained Oklahoma 307-71 in the first half and 521-359 overall against a defense that ranked 11th nationally in total defense and had not allowed more than 382 yards in a game all season. item.title: Julian Ward has seen enough: He wants £33m deal for 27-year-old
item.description: Julian Ward has seen enough: He wants £33m deal for 27-year-old Liverpool have been busy improving their defensive options over the last few transfer windows. The club have had to wave goodbye to players like Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ibrahima Konate and Andy Robertson. And next summer it looks likely that Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez will be also departing. Reds’ recruiters have set about gathering top young players to replenish the backline. Giovanni Leoni and Jeremy Jacquet are the landmark centre-back arrivals with Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe also coming in. And while those players are top prospects for the future there is a risk of a lack of experience being exposed. That’s why a deal for a senior defender makes sense. Liverpool want permanent Araujo deal Last summer the club completed a loan deal for Ronald Araujo - Barcelona’s 27-year-old centre-back cum right-back. The Uruguayan stopper has been an immediate hit with the Anfield faithful - leading to calls for him to be signed on a permanent basis. Liverpool have got an option to buy the defender for around £46m at the end of the season - a move that looks like a no-brainer considering his strong start. A report in Football Insider is claiming that decision-makers inside Anfield have already made up their minds - and a permanent deal will be pursued in 2027. Julian Ward wants HUGE discount on Araujo deal And now comes a report in Fichajes which claims the 2024/25 Premier League champions are seeking a significant reduction in the fee with Barca. “The Anfield club would like to close the deal for around 40 million euros, compared to the 55 million euro buy option,” the report reads. That price comes to around £33m at the current exchange rate - with Barcelona perhaps in a less than favourable negotiating position. The Blaugrana are desperate to offload Araujo - in order to generate some much-needed transfer income and to remove his mammoth salary from the books. A deal with Liverpool - even at a discounted rate - looks to be the optimum solution. Araujo isn’t in the usual age bracket for a Liverpool defensive signing - particularly in the last few seasons - but his experience will be invaluable going forward. It is definitely worth asking the question to Barcelona as to whether or not they would be willing to include a discount in the final deal.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 4 and 45 in two games against New Zealand before missing the next two. The head coach said players with strong long-term records deserve a longer rope. Gautam Gambhir hits back at critics over Vaibhav Sooryavanshi snub in 4th & 5th T20Is vs NZ Gautam Gambhir has made it clear that keeping everybody happy is not part of his job description while responding to critics who questioned the decision to leave out Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. The young left-hander was not part of the XI for the fourth and fifth T20Is against New Zealand, and it is a call that has drawn a lot of noise on social media. Sooryavanshi had been given his chance in the second and third matches of the series after Ishan Kishan was ruled out through injury. He made 4 in the first of those two games and then smashed 45 from 19 balls in India’s six-wicket win in the third T20I, an innings that made many fans believe he had done enough to hold his place. Instead, Kishan came back from his injury for the fourth game in Auckland, and Sooryavanshi sat out. Kishan was dismissed for a three-ball duck as India were bowled out for 172 while chasing a huge target of 260. The team management then stuck with the same top-order combination for the final match in Hamilton. However, the social media noise is bound to grow louder with both Indian openers, Abhishek Sharma (1) and Sanju Samson (4), departing cheaply in the 5th T20I in Hamilton. MORE: 'Not doing justice': Yuvraj wants Abhishek, Ishan and Vaibhav in India's ODI squad BCCI/Creimas What did Gautam Gambhir say about Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's omission? Gambhir spoke about the pressure of public opinion, the need for security in the dressing room and the faith he places in players who have performed over a long period. “First of all, my job is not to make everyone happy. My job is to take the right decisions, not the popular decisions. And that is what I’m there for," the coach opined. “I think sometimes in today’s day and age with so much of social media and all that chatter, what happens on the outside. No, it is very easy to take the popular decision. But for me, I think the important thing is to take the right decision and make sure that there is a lot of security inside the dressing room.” Finally, he turned to the talent question that had been put to him and explained why some players get more time than others. He said: “Because as you just mentioned that there’s a lot of talent. But again, I think guys have done phenomenally well over a longer period of time. Obviously deserves a longer rope. item.description: Jaime Chapman scored a first-half hat-trick for Australia against Wales [Getty Images] Australia (60) 124 Tries: Kernick, Chapman 6, Church 2, Southwell, Sergis 4, Apps, Paki, Joseph 2, Upton 2, Nizza Goals: Southwell 20 Wales (0) 6 Tries: Travis Goals: Preston Rampant Australia racked up the biggest score in international history as they hammered Wales in a Rugby League World Cup mismatch. The Jillaroos, hunting a fourth successive title, ran in 21 tries in a predictably lopsided contest in Sydney. The half-time score of 60-0 was the biggest of any World Cup match - men's or women's - and the Australians kept their foot down to win 124-6. Wing Jaime Chapman's sixth try in the last minute ensured they beat Denmark men's biggest international score of 122-8 against Sweden in 2012. The 118-point victory margin is the largest in any women's match, although France men retain their record win set in 2003 with a 120-0 rout of Serbia. Yet there were wild Wales celebrations when, at 100-0 down, they became the first side to score against the Jillaroos in the tournament through Paige Travis. The Jillaroos are three-time back-to-back champions, while Wales were taking part in the tournament for the first time having only played their first Test in 2021. It was just their 16th fixture - and a first against Australia - with Tom Brindle's side having already been beaten 70-6 by England and 76-0 by Samoa at the World Cup. Full of NRLW talent, Australia showed a killer instinct and an intensity that Wales were exposed to for the first time. Jessica Sergis scored one of Australia's 10 converted tries in the first half against Wales [Getty Images] It all came after Wales, whose captain Bethan Dainton was the tournament's top tackler by a distance in the first two rounds with 77, rose to the occasion with a strong start. item.title: Historical Footage Shows How Ridiculous Checked Swings Used to Be
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 13: Manager Dave Roberts of the Los Angeles Dodgers discuses a challenge with umpire James Hoye during the fourth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game one of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 13, 2025 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty In baseball, checked swings are as much of an art as they are a science. And most art has no rules, only trends. The checked swing has always been one of baseball’s more subjective calls, if not the most subjective – but in light of the controversy over one in the 2026 World Series, footage available online from the fall classic from 61 years previously illustrates just how much the interpretation has changed over the years. And it is a lot . A clip posted to YouTube shows several swings from the era that, by modern standards, would be difficult to describe as anything other than full attempts at hitting the ball. Yet they were treated as checked swings, with batters apparently getting away with movements that would absolutely certainly be called strikes in today’s game. Batters, it seems, could get completely fooled and get away with it. The footage is a good illustration of how baseball’s unwritten conventions can evolve without any corresponding change to the official rulebook. In fact, the interesting thing about checked swings is that the rulebook has never actually provided a precise definition of one. Read More From Heavy Former Dodgers Mainstay Wants to Make a Comeback No One Really Knows What A Checked Swing Is As has been made very well known in the aftermath of the World Series , under MLB’s Official Baseball Rules, there is no specific definition of a checked swing. Nor is there a written standard stating exactly how far a batter can move the bat before an attempt becomes a swing. The rulebook’s definition of a strike includes a pitch at which the batter swings and misses, with the relevant wording referring to a pitch that is “struck at by the batter”. But what constitutes being “struck at” is ultimately left to the umpire’s judgement. There is a provision in Rule 8.02(c) that allows the defensive team to appeal a half-swing on a pitch initially called a ball. The home-plate umpire can ask the first- or third-base umpire for assistance, depending on which side the batter is hitting from. However, this provision explains how an appeal is handled, rather than establishing a measurable definition of a swing. That, then, leaves umpires relying on their own interpretation. And while that is by design, it also is a system that leaves nobody being quite happy about it. Commonly cited standards include whether the batter breaks his wrists, whether the bat crosses the plate, or whether the barrel moves far enough forward to constitute an attempt. item.title: Jose Mourinho makes decision on starting right-back for Real Madrid against Racing Santander – report
item.description: Jose Mourinho makes decision on starting right-back for Real Madrid against Racing Santander – report Real Madrid find themselves in an interesting position with regard to their right-back dilemma ahead of the Racing Santander clash. Jose Mourinho decided to start Federico Valverde at right-back in recent games to give the team better balance. Los Blancos ‘ fortunes have changed since then, and this has left Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold with limited game time. Now, according to Diario AS , Dumfries is expected to start against Racing Santander on Sunday, ahead of the Englishman. Jose Mourinho is leaning towards giving the Dutchman his starting spot back as he looks to balance the minutes across the squad. Dumfries set to get the nod ahead of Trent The decision comes after captain Valverde was ruled out of the trip to El Sardinero due to lingering muscular discomfort. While Real Madrid confirmed that the Uruguayan midfielder hadn’t suffered an injury, his absence from training this week meant Mourinho didn’t want to take any chances. Denzel Dumfries is expected to start against Racing Santander. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) In the Clasico , Dumfries replaced his captain at around the hour mark, and Mourinho seems pretty clear on the pecking order at right-back. As things stand, the Dutchman is the backup to Fede Valverde and will get the first opportunity ahead of Trent. For the Englishman, this situation has become increasingly frustrating. He arrived from Liverpool with enormous expectations, but his Real Madrid career just hasn’t taken off. Jose Mourinho admitted that he was disappointed to find himself in this unfortunate situation but that both players understood it was for the greater good of the team. Where does Alexander-Arnold go from here? Dumfries and Trent are two contrasting right-backs whose strengths and weaknesses are quite different. Trent Alexander-Arnold finds himself in a difficult position at Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Against Racing, a side who like to attack, Mourinho might be of the opinion that Dumfries offers more value than Trent. Even if he doesn’t start tonight against Racing, Trent will hope to come off the bench and make an impression. A good display could earn him a chance against AEK Athens or Valencia next weekend, and it remains to be seen how Mourinho sets his team up against Racing tonight.

item.title: Joan Garcia talks Farinas, high defensive line, Atletico Madrid and more after Barcelona 6-1 Alaves
item.description: Joan Garcia talks Farinas, high defensive line, Atletico Madrid and more after Barcelona 6-1 Alaves FC Barcelona came back to winning ways on Saturday evening thanks to a resounding performance that saw them secure a 6-1 victory over Deportivo Alaves. The dominant night saw Lamine Yamal and Raphinha both score a brace, though Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia will be disappointed not to have retained a clean sheet, as Alaves’ Mariano Diaz scored a late goal. Speaking to the media after the game, Garcia talked about the response to a difficult week, his makeshift defence and the fine margins that cost them against Europe’s elite. Garcia’s view on Barcelona performance Garcia was delighted with the manner of the bounce-back, even though a late goal denied him a clean sheet. It was a dominant display from Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “We did our job. We were focused and played well. We had to respond after the tough week we had with two defeats. We’re still top of the league ,” he said. “We have to keep a cool head to stay in first place. As for the goal we conceded? Every goalkeeper will tell you the same thing, that they want a clean sheet, but the important thing is to win,” he added. Garcia will take the result, especially after a trying weekend against Real Madrid, where he conceded two goals. Praise for de Jong and Farinas The goalkeeper reserved special mention for Frenkie de Jong and Brian Farinas, both of who also received praise from Hansi Flick for their strong performances in rather unfamiliar roles. “It was a somewhat unusual defensive line for us. But Frenkie and Brian showed great character and demonstrated how good they are as players. Brian had a very good game in a difficult match because it wasn’t his usual position ,” he said (h/t Mundo Deportivo ). “He showed the personality he has. And Frenkie gives us a lot on the ball; he almost never loses it. Good players can perform well regardless of their position. That’s exactly what they both showed today. I’m very happy for them ,” he added. Lots of learning When asked about the recent defeats to PSG and Real Madrid, Garcia pinpointed small details as the difference. “Against these great teams like PSG and Real Madrid, everything comes down to details at the end. item.title: More than a sidekick! Bundesliga youngster must escape endless comparisons
item.description: More than a sidekick! Bundesliga youngster must escape endless comparisons "I won't make it to the very top of world football. My ceiling was lower—but that ceiling was still the Bundesliga," Felix Kroos wrote about the endless comparisons with his brother Toni. Your own achievements do not become any less significant just because someone else reaches even greater heights. Malek El Mala would do well to remember those words as he potentially makes his Bundesliga debut for Köln today. The 21-year-old is also living in someone else's shadow. Dismissed as the brother you simply have to sign for the youth team if you want to get your hands on Saïd. That was the story circulating in the summer, when talk turned to the astronomical fee last Bundesliga season's breakout star might be sold for. Malek El Mala, the add-on. That was how he was seen for a long time, but now he is on the verge of stepping onto football's biggest stage himself. He has earned it in his own right. Given the constant pressure to deliver results, no professional coach can be accused of handing out squad places lightly. El Mala has already been named in the squad for two first-team matches, but has yet to come off the bench. That could change today against Union Berlin, his coach René Wagner hinted at the press conference: "In Malek, we have an out-and-out number nine in the squad who will have a role to play in games where we need that specific position." He is benefiting from Köln's injury situation. Ragnar Ache, Thijs Dallinga and Imad Rondic are all out, opening the door to the first team. But that is nothing unusual for young players: most benefit at some point from established options being unavailable through injury or a dip in form. 📸 Christof Koepsel - 2025 Getty Images An opportunity he earned himself Even so, you have to put yourself forward at the right moment to get your chance. El Mala has scored five goals in eleven Regionalliga appearances. Most recently, he netted three times in two matches. In other words, he has put himself in a position to become an option for Wagner. He is still very young. Twenty-one. A good age to develop and take your first steps in professional football. For Wagner, the reason it has not happened sooner is obvious: "We all know Malek's story. He's had a few injury problems along the way." But now the breakthrough is supposed to come: "Malek is knocking ever louder on the door," Wagner said, according to 'Express', after last Tuesday's cup victory, which also came against Union Berlin. The coach also believes in a successful future for him: "We mustn't forget that Malek is still at the beginning of his career. If he keeps this up, his time will definitely come. Perhaps very soon." Not everyone can take off the way Saïd El Mala did last season. Many young players need more patience and have to work hard for their playing time. item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images VJ Edgecombe pulled off a clutch three-pointer for the second game running to help the Philadelphia 76ers go 6-1. Edgecombe scored a clutch triple against the Knicks in the NBA Cup before doing the exact same thing against the Hornets on Halloween night. However, just before he took the shot, he had a different plan. He said on NBCS Philly after the game: “I told him, he looked at me to pass me the ball. I said: ‘Don’t pass me the ball. That’s what you do. item.description: PSV manager Peter Bosz admitted he hesitated before informing his players that Feyenoord had dropped points against Fortuna Sittard, but ultimately decided to use the result as extra motivation ahead of their emphatic victory over Willem II. Peter Bosz had plenty of reasons to be satisfied after PSV Eindhoven dismantled Willem II 7-0 on Saturday evening . The victory strengthened their position in the Eredivisie title race, improved their goal difference and provided an ideal platform ahead of their Champions League meeting with Club Brugge. However, one detail behind the preparations for the match caught particular attention. Bosz revealed that he had informed his players about Feyenoord's 1-1 draw against Fortuna Sittard before kick-off, despite initially questioning whether doing so might distract his squad. “Yes, though I did have my doubts. I wondered if it might be a distraction,” Bosz explained. “My only concern was that one or two players might take this match too lightly, or perhaps have their minds already on the Brugge game. I figured I'd use every tool at my disposal to keep the pressure on the squad, by pointing out that the Feyenoord match had ended in a 1-1 draw.” The decision appeared to have the desired effect. PSV secured a convincing victory, scoring seven goals without conceding. The result also transformed the goal-difference picture, with Feyenoord's advantage of six goals over PSV overturned . “Winning is what matters, and the fact that it's a big scoreline? That's a bonus,” Bosz said. He also highlighted the importance of keeping a clean sheet, although he acknowledged that Willem II came close to scoring when they struck the crossbar. item.description: Simeone equals Luis Aragonés’s LaLiga wins record as Atlético Madrid beat Levante 2-0 Atlético Madrid won 2-0 at Levante on Saturday, making it a milestone afternoon for Diego Simeone. The hosts’ expected goals reached 1.33, against 0.63 for the visitors. Jan Oblak was the difference. Around the tenth minute, he made a crucial one-handed save to deny Dani Requena, Infobae (EFE) reported. The goalkeeper finished with a rating of 8.08. Atlético had more of the ball, with 54% possession and 560 passes to Levante’s 450. Simeone made two double changes. Jonathan David and Sørloth replaced Lee Kang-In and Julián Álvarez in the 67th minute. Le Normand and Lookman came on for Barrios and Baena in the 76th. The result was Atlético’s seventh league win in a row. It briefly took them top of the table. The teams’ last meeting, on 31 January 2026, had ended 0-0 in Valencia. Barcelona’s visit could give Simeone the record outright Simeone already leads Aragonés on wider measures at the club. Across all official competitions with Atlético, he has 479 wins from 813 games. Aragonés managed 308 wins from 612 games there. The club credits Simeone with eight trophies as coach, two more than Aragonés’s six. The coming weeks carry real weight. From 11 games, Atlético have nine wins, one draw and one defeat. Real Madrid sit third on 24 points from 10 games. Levante are 17th on 10 points after their second straight defeat.
